rationale: openai/gpt-oss-20b is shipped. It sits exactly on the twenty billion parameter cap the problem statement sets, it is served in production by the configured provider, and it accepts strict json_schema constrained decoding, so the plan it returns is shaped by the contract rather than by prompting alone. That matters more here than raw capability: the model's only job is to turn a question into a QueryPlan, and a plan that fails validation is retried once and then refused. Llama 3.1 8B Instant is faster and cheaper and is the fallback worth testing when latency matters more than coverage; Llama 4 Scout has seventeen billion active parameters and sits between them. Because every figure is computed in DuckDB and checked against allowed_numbers before it is shown, a weaker model produces a clarification or a refusal rather than a wrong number, so the choice trades coverage against latency and never against correctness. THE PER-MODEL ACCURACY BELOW HAS NOT YET BEEN MEASURED AGAINST THE LIVE ENDPOINT. The figures are carried over from the fixture this file shipped with and are placeholders. Running eval/run_benchmark.py replaces them; it needs a provider allowance large enough for three models over forty-four questions, which the free tier's two hundred thousand tokens a day does not cover.
